title: Taylor OKs data center and power plant campus amid resident opposition
key_facts: Taylor City Council unanimously approved on Thursday (8 Oct 2026) an economic development agreement with Big Watt Digital LLC (South Dakota) and PowerHouse Data Centers (Virginia) for a 660-acre data centre and natural gas power plant campus, annexing it into the city.

The campus, the Taylor Technology Campus (formerly Project Mustang), will have 500 MW of data centre capacity with an option for another 500 MW, powered by an on-site gas plant, not connected to the grid, with the option to sell power back.

The agreement requires a one-time fill of 1.575 million gallons of reclaimed water in a closed-loop cooling system, setbacks of 300 to 700 feet from property lines, and lets the city suspend or end the project if rules are broken.
The developers promised at least $28.2 million to the community; the agreement offers no tax breaks or incentives.
Developers say the project will generate about $4.8 billion in economic output for Williamson County, more than 19,000 temporary construction jobs and about 320 permanent jobs.
Public comment at the tense meeting was dominated by opposition; residents asked for a pause until state officials finish their review of data centres.
Gov. Greg Abbott ordered the TCEQ in September to halt data centre permits pending a statewide review; Austin is weighing a ban on large data centres and San Marcos approved one in June.
quote_evidence: Taylor City Council unanimously approved an economic development agreement with South Dakota-based Big Watt Digital LLC and Virginia-based PowerHouse Data Centers on their joint 660-acre data center and natural gas power plant campus.
The agreement offers no tax breaks or incentives for the developers.
why_it_matters_hint: A big gas-powered campus approved over local opposition while Texas reviews data centre permits.
notes: Job and revenue figures are the developers' estimates.
